links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 12, Designing and Deploying Command Line Programs
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: the terminal, PATH, virtual environments, pip, text-based design, launchers and PyInstaller.

links.title: sys — System-specific parameters and functions
links.why: sys.argv, sys.exit and its exit codes, sys.executable, sys.platform and sys.version_info.

links.title: venv — Creation of virtual environments
links.why: What python -m venv creates, what activation changes, and the sys.prefix test for an environment.

links.title: argparse — Parser for command-line options, arguments and subcommands
links.why: The module the chapter recommends once arguments multiply, and leaves to its documentation.

links.title: shlex — Simple lexical analysis
links.why: shlex.split splits a typed command line the way a POSIX shell does, quotation marks included.

links.title: os — Miscellaneous operating system interfaces
links.why: os.name, os.system, os.chdir and os.getcwd, used by the clear() one-liner and ccwd.

links.title: shutil — High-level file operations
links.why: shutil.which, the Python form of the which and where commands.

links.title: User Guide - pip documentation
links.why: Why pip is run as python -m pip, and the install, list and uninstall commands.

links.title: Using PyInstaller
links.why: --onefile and --onedir, the build and dist folders and the spec file.

links.title: PEP 405 – Python Virtual Environments
links.why: Carl Meyer's 2011 proposal that made virtual environments part of Python 3.3.

links.title: PEP 668 – Marking Python base environments as externally managed
links.why: Why pip install into the system Python now stops with externally-managed-environment.
